Latency: p95 <= 350ms for 512-token requests on Dedicated config (measured over 1 hour sustained run)
Throughput: sustained 200 req/s with <=2% error rate for 30-minute run (burst to 400 req/s tolerated)
Cost: per-inference token cost within 20% of Redwood baseline estimate (report to include token counts and raw cost calc)
Stability: no more than 3 availability incidents (5+ min) during 3-week POC

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-03
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Alex Murphy (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (CTO, StellarPay), Mark Chen (Infra Lead), Liam O'Connor (Product)

Summary (auto): POC success criteria and acceptance tests reviewed and agreed. Customer to provide prompt set and traces; Redwood will run baseline + quantized benchmarks and share results. Timeline: 3-week POC with signoff criteria spelled out. Security docs to be delivered.

00:00 Alex: okay good afternoon everyone thanks for joining, this is Alex from Redwood, I have Priya who is our solutions engineer here as well.
00:08 Sofia: hey thanks Alex, we got your calendar — looks good, we wanted to lock down the success criteria before we spin up infra.
00:14 Priya: great, we'll go through the acceptance tests and the reporting format, and then outline the bench matrix and timeline. quick note, transcription may have a few mis-hearings — sorry if names get munged.
00:25 Mark: fine. quick context: we're evaluating for payment fraud triage and chat support routing, throughput is important — we need low-latency for live chat, and also batch scoring overnight.
00:36 Alex: perfect. two things we'll lock: quality thresholds and performance thresholds, and then the go/no-go pass rules. does that match your ask Sofia?
00:45 Sofia: yep. oh and security: SOC2, SSO, KMS for keys, and we need VPC peering or Private deployment.
00:53 Priya: noted — we'll include Private deployment network diagram in the artifacts. for the POC we'll offer a sandbox VPC peering with customer-managed keys for tokens if you need.
01:05 Liam: also curious about cost — if dedicated GPU pricing is much higher than hosted, that's a blocker.
01:12 Alex: totally, cost is one of our acceptance criteria, we'll measure token-level cost and compare to the baseline estimate. if it exceeds 20% of the estimate that's a discussion point, not an auto-fail — but we log it.
01:25 Priya: moving to specifics: quality acceptance — we suggest a human-eval on a 100-prompt sample set you provide. pass = 90% of samples scoring >= 4 out of 5 on relevance and correctness, measured blind by two raters.
01:38 Sofia: ok 100 prompts is doable. for fraud triage some prompts are long (up to 1k tokens) — can we scope both 512 and 1024 token ranges?
01:47 Priya: yes, we'll run separate buckets: short (<=512) and long (512-1024). note that latency p95 will differ; we set p95 target at 350ms for 512, and 700ms for 1024 on Dedicated config as a rough goal. we can tighten during tuning.
02:02 Mark: just to clarify, 350ms p95 — is that cold start or steady-state?
02:06 Priya: steady-state, after KV cache is warmed and using batching tuned to your traffic distribution. cold-start isn't part of the POC SLA but we'll measure it.
02:15 Alex: also throughput goal — you said live chat; what's your target concurrent users / reqs per second?
02:20 Mark: live traffic is about 150 RPS at peak with bursts to 300 — but many are short requests ~200 tokens. batch scoring overnight is 2M requests over 6 hours.
02:31 Priya: for the POC we recommend a sustained 200 req/s test for 30 minutes with <=2% error rate, and a 1-hour stress test up to 400 req/s to validate autoscaling. batch run we'll model with a 6h run at average throughput as well.
02:45 Liam: on the quality side, we also want FDR (false detection rate) to not increase more than 5% compared to baseline heuristic.
02:52 Alex: that's a product metric we'll capture — we can ingest your labelled baseline and compute delta. good point.
03:00 Sofia: benchmarks — what's the reporting format? CSV? dashboards?
03:04 Priya: we'll provide a CSV export (schema we'll share) with per-request latencies, token counts, and cost per request. plus a 2-slide executive summary at the end. logs will be available for deep-dive.
03:15 (short pause)
03:18 Mark: security again, do you support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via KMS?
03:22 Priya: yes, we support KMS/HSM integrations in Private and Dedicated; for hosted we can support customer-managed keys in a limited fashion. we'll share the security pack.
03:32 Sofia: SSO? audit logs? retention controls?
03:36 Alex: yes, SAML SSO supported, RBAC at token level and audit logs exportable. retention controls can be configured on the POC sandbox.
03:45 Priya: now acceptance tests — we propose the following pass rules (tied to benchmarks):
03:51 Priya: 1) Quality: >= 90% on 100 prompts (human-eval). 2) Latency: p95 <= 350ms for <=512 tokens. 3) Throughput: sustained 200 req/s <=2% errors. 4) Cost: tokens cost within 20% of estimate. 5) Stability: no more than 3 incidents.
04:11 Sofia: sounds fair. if we fail any single item is that an automatic no-go?
04:16 Alex: we treat quality and stability as hard gates — if quality or stability fail it's a no-go. latency and cost are soft gates — can be mitigated by configuration (quantization, batching) and we allow one tuning cycle before final decision.
04:30 Liam: what's the tuning cycle length?
04:33 Priya: 1 week of tuning — we run quantized variants, different batching and KV cache settings. we'll re-run the benchmarks at end of that week.
04:41 Mark: timeline overall?
04:43 Alex: suggested: Week 0 (this week) — signoff on criteria and infra provisioning; Week 1 — integration + baseline runs; Week 2 — tuning + quantized runs; Week 3 — final validation + report and signoff. total 3 weeks active.
04:59 Sofia: agree. for infra we'll need a network diagram and egress estimate for finance.
05:05 Alex: we'll send network diagram, expected egress and a cost worksheet.
05:10 (gentle cross talk)
05:12 Priya: on benchmarks — we'll run baseline (float32) and two quantized variants (4-bit and 8-bit) where supported. we'll record token-level quality delta so you can see tradeoffs.
05:24 Mark: does Redwood support model fallbacks if a variant fails quality?
05:28 Priya: yes, smart routing can fall back to a higher-quality variant in real-time. for the POC we'll demonstrate canary fallback for a small percent of traffic.
05:36 Sofia: are we allowed to bring our own model for testing? some of our research has in-house fine-tuned checkpoints.
05:41 Alex: we can host customer-provided models in Dedicated or Private — we'll need licensing confirmation and a quick security review. for the POC we can do a sandbox.
05:50 Liam: results delivery format — you mentioned CSV, can you also push to our S3?
05:53 Priya: yes, secure S3 transfer is fine, or we can share via a pre-signed link over our secure console.
06:00 (brief pause)
06:05 Sofia: ok let's capture next steps and assign owners.
06:08 Alex: I'll take benchmarks template and pricing. Priya will provision the test endpoint and run baseline tests. Sofia will provide prompt set and traces. Mark will confirm network constraints.
06:20 Alex: any other blockers?
06:22 Mark: procurement timeline — procurement needs 2 weeks after POC signoff.
06:26 Alex: noted. we'll make the final report concise for procurement.
06:30 Sofia: one more question: do you expose token breakdowns per API call? we need that for accounting.
06:35 Priya: yes, token_in and token_out for each request in CSV.
06:39 Liam: good. that should cover it.
06:42 Alex: perfect. we'll email the artifact bundle: benchmark template, security pack, network diagram, and draft pricing.
06:49 Sofia: thanks everyone.
06:51 Alex: thanks — talk soon.

Post-call recap (auto): Agreement on POC acceptance criteria, timeline, and deliverables. Action items assigned. Redwood to run baseline and quantized benchmarks and produce CSV + slide summaries. Customer to deliver prompt/test data and confirm networking.
